title: Roblox client-server authority and remotes
summary: A platform capability area covering client-server communication and validation of consequential requests at the server boundary.

designKnowledge.verifiedScope: Official Creator Hub documentation describes remote communication and the client-server security boundary. Verify exact API behavior against current documentation before a version-specific implementation.
authorityQuestions: What is a client request versus an accepted result?
Which types, ownership, range, permissions, state, and rate are validated?
How do observers learn about the accepted result?
designKnowledge.securityBoundary: Clients can be modified or send arbitrary requests. Client-side checks and UI state are not security controls for consequential game state.

technicalPatterns.name: Validate every consequential request
technicalPatterns.guidance: At the server, check types and bounds, ownership, permission, distance, current phase, resource cost, cooldown, and request rate before changing state.

technicalPatterns.name: Replicate accepted outcomes
technicalPatterns.guidance: Keep authority and presentation separate. Client prediction may improve feel, but server-confirmed outcomes determine shared state.

technicalPatterns.name: Bound remote contracts
technicalPatterns.guidance: Define payload shape, size, frequency, error behavior, and idempotency for each remote interaction.

failureModes.description: A server accepts client-supplied damage, ownership, position, or reward without validation.
failureModes.mitigation: Reconstruct the result from server-owned state and validate each request against current game state.

failureModes.description: Remote traffic triggers unbounded processing or expensive world queries.
failureModes.mitigation: Apply rate limits, payload bounds, cancellation, and measured work budgets.

scenarios.action: Submit wrong types, out-of-range values, unauthorized targets, stale state, and repeated requests.
scenarios.expected: The server rejects invalid requests without changing consequential state or producing excessive work.

scenarios.action: Perform one valid shared action and inspect server and observer state.
scenarios.expected: The server changes state once and both clients observe the accepted result.

acceptanceCriteria: Authority is declared per state field.
Remote payloads and rates are bounded.
Adversarial client cases are tested in an unpublished local Studio session.

considerations: Measure remote frequency, payload, server work, and replication cost at the expected player count.
A local multi-client run does not prove live network reliability or persistence.

evidence.description: Current official remote and security documentation is linked to bounded implementation and adversarial testing patterns.

assumptions: The cited documentation is version-sensitive and must be rechecked at implementation time.
This record does not certify any implementation as secure.
